memos.scout:
The strongest honest case for buying is thin. The brief shows real participation: 1,905 buyers and about 332k USD of volume in the last 15 minutes, a graduation with 1,010 non-agent buyers in the first two minutes, and a top-5 buyer share of only 8.7%, which argues against a single whale-driven pump. The coin is alive, and the pool holds about 205 SOL, so a $20 ticket would have modest impact.

But the flow has turned. Net flow over the last 15 minutes is -14.5 SOL, with sellers (1,603) and sell volume (1,412 SOL) nearly matching buys, and the price is down 32% in that window and 38% off its 30-minute high. A sell-to-buy ratio of 0.93 in the launch window means early buyers were already exiting. Bundle share of 40.6% and a 25% completer share point to coordinated early activity, which is a warning sign rather than evidence of durable demand. The 3.4x return over 30 minutes means much of the move is already behind us.

My verdict: there is no strong case for buying now. Demand was real at launch but has rotated into selling, and the base rates for buying into a fading coin 30 minutes after graduation are poor. Skip it unless the brief showed net buying returning, which it does not.
memos.skeptic: Most likely loss: distribution into the bid after a 3.4x run. The coin is down 38% from its 30-minute high (drawdown 0.3843), and the last 15 minutes show sells of 1,412 SOL against buys of 1,398, a net outflow of -14.5 SOL with 1,603 sellers versus 1,905 buyers. That is sustained exit flow, not a shakeout. Pool depth is only 204.7 SOL, so a $20 round trip costing 1.4-5.1% gets worse on any move that is thin, and the sell pressure can push price down faster than we can exit. The curve data adds risk: bundle share is 40.5% and top-3 holders hold 21.9%, suggesting coordinated buying that can coordinate selling. The launch bot and sell-to-buy ratio of 0.93 in the first two minutes point the same way. Base rates say this profile loses, so I'd pass.
